evaluations.evidence: As a moderator, I want to create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Creating a new game is a self-contained feature and does not require other backlog stories to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators by providing a URL inherently requires a game (and its URL) to exist first (creation of games).

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item
evaluations.rationale: Starting a round presupposes an existing game/session in which the round occurs, so it depends on game creation.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Showing all session items depends on items having been created (e.g., via adding items or starting rounds).

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item to estimate requires that items exist (added or created in earlier rounds), so it depends on item creation features.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding items is scoped to a game/session; it inherently requires a game context to add items into (game creation).

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item presupposes that items can be added/found (depends on add-item functionality).

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item requires that items exist (added previously), so it depends on the add-item story.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: This is a behavior choice for the estimate-display flow and can be implemented without requiring a specific other backlog story to be completed first.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average is a self-contained moderator action/operation and does not inherently require another backlog story implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Auto-fill behavior is an independent UI/logic feature that can be implemented without depending on a specific other backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering an agreed estimate is a standalone moderator action and does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating a prior story requires access to the list/history of session items or selecting previous items, so it depends on prior-items and selection features.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing stories is a self-contained ingestion feature and does not inherently require other backlog stories to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste import is a standalone input feature and does not inherently depend on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games requires that games have been created and stored (game creation and persistence).

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game, so that I can see the stories and estimates
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a transcript depends on game/session data (stories and estimates) having been recorded—i.e., games must exist and be persisted.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript requires the transcript/view feature to exist (stored transcript), so it depends on viewing/storing transcripts.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: CSV export depends on having game transcripts stored/available (the transcript feature).

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game presumes stored games exist; therefore it depends on game creation/persistence.

evaluations.evidence: create an account for the application by entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Account creation is a self-contained feature and does not inherently require other backlog stories first.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Logging in necessarily requires accounts to exist (account creation).

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Changing account details depends on having an account (and typically being able to authenticate), so it depends on account creation/login.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Account deletion presupposes accounts exist; it depends on account creation and on the ability to associate stored games with accounts.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Timezone display is a UI/formatting concern that can be implemented independently.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminder requires accounts and stored credential data, so it depends on account creation/persistence.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Selecting the card set is a standalone configuration choice and does not require other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Limiting invites to 15 is a constraint on the invite mechanism and therefore depends on the invitation feature.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining a game presupposes that a game and an access URL exist (invitation and creation features).

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: To see the current item requires that a round/item has been started or selected, so it depends on round/item creation/selection features.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Participant view of all session items depends on those items being created and exposed (moderator item-list features).

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Displaying who has submitted an estimate is a UI/behavioral feature that can be implemented without a specific other backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: This describes the core reveal behavior and does not inherently require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate prior to reveal is an independent participant interaction requirement.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Showing prior per-estimator estimates requires stored history and navigation to prior rounds, so it depends on the ability to view/scroll prior rounds.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Showing who gave which estimates in the current round is a presentational feature that can be implemented independently of other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Timer functionality is self-contained and does not inherently depend on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Timer reset behavior can be implemented as part of the timer/round logic without requiring a separate backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Scrolling through prior rounds is a stored-session navigation feature that can be implemented without dependency on a different backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Card-order consistency is an independent UI requirement.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Ability to change an estimate during an active draw is an interaction requirement that does not inherently depend on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying thumbnails is a presentational/profile feature that can be implemented independently (no concrete dependency specified).

evaluations.evidence: site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is a general non-functional requirement that does not inherently depend on other stories.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Providing a glossary is self-contained and does not require other backlog stories first.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Creating database indexes is a developer task that can be implemented independently.

evaluations.evidence: application function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Cross-browser compatibility is a non-functional requirement that does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is a non-functional requirement and can be implemented independently.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance/responsiveness is an independent quality requirement, not inherently dependent on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a self-contained technical requirement.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design is independent and does not inherently require other stories to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error page design is a self-contained UI/UX requirement.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Storing anonymized results presupposes that results are recorded/stored (transcript/storage features), so it depends on data persistence/transcript capabilities.

evaluations.evidence: be able to see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Metrics/analytics can be implemented as an independent feature; no concrete backlog story is required beforehand.
